subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should OpenClaw accept skill lifecycle optimization and retirement in core, expose the needed hooks for a plugin/ClawHub implementation, or defer the feature?
rationale: The remaining work changes user-owned skill state, public config, persistence, ranking, and deletion/restore semantics; code inspection shows no narrow bug fix can choose those policies safely.

options.title: Design core/plugin lifecycle API
options.body: Define a small approved boundary for skill usage metrics, repair proposal provenance, archive/restore state, and user-confirmed deletion before any implementation PR.

options.title: Keep as ClawHub/plugin direction
options.body: Route lifecycle management to an external plugin or ClawHub package and only add core APIs if the current surfaces cannot support it.

options.title: Defer retirement behavior
options.body: Keep the current Skill Workshop correction capture and postpone automated archive/delete behavior until stronger user demand or maintainer sponsorship exists.

recommendation.title: Design core/plugin lifecycle API
recommendation.body: Define a small approved boundary for skill usage metrics, repair proposal provenance, archive/restore state, and user-confirmed deletion before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Skill Workshop product/UX changes make steipete the strongest available owner for deciding whether this belongs in core or an extension boundary.
